hints: Identify that for $f$ to be increasing for all $x > n$, we must have $n \ge 4$, so least integer $n = 4$.
walkthrough:
An increasing function requires $f'(x) \ge 0$ across its entire domain $x > n$:
$$f'(x) = x^2 - 6x + 8 \ge 0$$

For the function to be increasing on the single uninterrupted domain $x > n$, the interval must lie entirely within $x \ge 4$:
$$n \ge 4 \implies \text{Least possible integer value: } n = 4$$
